MARTIAL LAW ORDERS By CHIEF MARTIAL LAW ADMINISTRATOR No
MARTIAL LAW ORDERS BY CHIEF MARTIAL
LAW
ADMINISTRATOR No. 102
[Gazette of
Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 12th January, 1985]
Whereas it is expedient that the
forthcoming elections may be held in peaceful atmosphere and during the process
no law and order problem is caused ;
And whereas it is also necessary
that candidates for election to a Provincial Assembly or the National Assembly
may be afforded equal chance and full opportunity to, propagate their cause and
to secure the support of the electorate ;
And whereas for this purpose it
is necessary to regulate and lay down the rules of the game or, in; other
words, the Code of Conduct for Electioneering ;
Now, therefore, the Chief Martial
Law Administrator is pleased to promulgate the following Martial Law Order :-
1. This Order shall come into
force at once and shall have effect notwithstanding anything contained in any
law for the time being in force including a Martial Law Regulation or Order.
2. No person who is a candidate
for election to a Provincial Assembly or the National Assembly, or any other
person on behalf or in support of such person, shall-
(a) hold or
cause to be held any meeting of public nature for securing or enlisting support
in his favour of in favour of such person ;
(b) take out or
cause to be taken out any procession of public nature for securing support in
his favour or in favour of such person ;
(c) use force,
violence, intimidation or threats of injury or offer monetary gains in
propagating 'or for securing support for himself or for such person ;
(d) in any
manner, cause injury or damage to any person or property ;
(e) in any
manner interfere with, or cause disruption, in the functioning of educational
institutions ;
(f) interfere in
the operation or the functioning of Public Services, Corporations or
Institutions set up by or under any law ;
(g) seduce, or
attempt to seduce, from allegiance to his duty, any public servant or any
person serving in any Corporation or any other institution set up by or under
any law ;
(h) prevent or
hinder any newsmedia from the performance of its function ;
(j) in any
manner, interfere with the functioning of, or transgress the limits of decent
and fair criticism in respect of any other candidate for election ; or
(k) in any
manner, by himself or by any other person, obstruct, hinder or propagate
against the holding of the elections.
3. No person shall participate in
any procession of a political nature or assist financially or in any other
manner whatsoever in the taking out of such procession or publicise or project
the same through newsmedia.
4. No person shall attend any
meeting of political and of public nature or assist, financially or in any
other manner whatsoever in the holding of such a meeting or publicise or
project the same through newsmedia.
5. No person shall do anything,
whether by committing an act or by words, either spoken or written, or by signs
or by visible representation or otherwise :-
(a) which is
calculated W create hatred against any religion, community, race, class, sect
or tribe or between people of different regions or holding different political
views and opinions ; or
(b) which is
calculated to incite the people to violence or to cause damage to any property.
6. Notwithstanding anything
contained in this Order, a person in connection with the forthcoming elections
may-
(a) hold close
door meetings in any place other than a building, structure, or enclosure of
any kind used by, or intended to be used by, or connected in any manner with,
any educational institution, place of public entertainment, worship or
religious sanctity ;
(b) hold close
door press conferences or give interviews to the press in the manner specified
in clause (a) ;
(c) individually
or through any other person approach electors for the purpose of enlisting
their support and may canvass for this purpose ; or
